Data Visualization Using ggplot2

Dr. N Anil Kumar

2025-11-11

Abstract

Effective data visualization is fundamental to exploratory data analysis, statistical inference, and the communication of analytical insights. This notebook reproduces the chapter “Data Visualization Using ggplot2” and provides runnable R code that implements the examples, visualizations, and workflows discussed in the chapter. The material proceeds from core principles (Grammar of Graphics) to categorical and numerical visualizations, bivariate relationships, multivariate techniques, and specialized plots using ggplot2 with light extensions (GGally, ggridges). The emphasis is on reproducible, publication-ready figures using theme_classic().

1.0 Introduction

This notebook accompanies the chapter text and contains executable code for the examples. Load required packages and set a consistent theme for publication-style plots.

library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
#library(GGally)
library(ggridges)
library(viridis) # for color scales where used
## Loading required package: viridisLite
options(repr.plot.width = 7, repr.plot.height = 5)
theme_set(theme_classic())

2.0 The Grammar of Graphics and ggplot2 Framework

A minimal example illustrating the layered grammar:

ggplot(data = mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Engine displacement vs highway mileage",
       x = "Engine displacement (litres)",
       y = "Highway miles per gallon")

3.0 Visualizing Relationships Between Numerical Variables

3.1 Basic scatter

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(caption = "Dataset: mpg (ggplot2)")

3.2 Aesthetic mappings: color & shape

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, color = drv, shape = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(title = "Displacement vs Highway MPG by Drive Type")

3.3 Adding smoothing / trend lines

# LOESS (default)
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, color = drv)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "LOESS smoothing by drive type")
## `geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'

# Linear model, no SE
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, color = drv, shape = drv)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Linear fit by drive type (se suppressed)")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

3.4 Labels, legends, and themes

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, color = drv, shape = drv)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Engine Displacement and Highway Fuel Efficiency",
    subtitle = "Comparison Across Drive Types",
    x = "Engine Displacement (litres)",
    y = "Highway Miles per Gallon",
    color = "Drive Type",
    shape = "Drive Type",
    caption = "Source: mpg dataset (ggplot2)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

4.0 Visualizing Categorical Variables

4.1 Single categorical: bar charts

# Simple counts by drive type
p1 <- ggplot(mpg, aes(x = drv)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Count by Drive Type")

p1

# flipped
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = drv)) +
  geom_bar() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Count by Drive Type (flipped)")

4.2 Fill aesthetics and alpha

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = class, fill = class)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Counts by Vehicle Class (fill=class)")

4.3 Ordering with forcats

# frequency order
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = fct_infreq(class))) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Vehicle class ordered by frequency")

4.4 Two categorical variables: stacked / dodge / fill

# stacked
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = class, fill = drv)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Stacked: Class by Drive Type")

# dodge
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = class, fill = drv)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Dodge: Class by Drive Type")

# fill (proportions)
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = class, fill = drv)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Proportions: Class by Drive Type")

4.5 Faceting for categorical comparisons

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = class, fill = drv)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~drv) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Faceted counts by drive type")

4.6 Example with diamonds dataset

data(diamonds)

ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = cut, fill = color)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Diamonds: Cut vs Color (dodge)")

5.0 Visualizing Distributions of Numerical Variables

5.1 Histogram & binwidth

set.seed(121)
abc_stock <- data.frame(price = rnorm(1000, mean = 300, sd = 10))

ggplot(abc_stock, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(title = "Histogram: Simulated stock price")
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

# adjusted binwidth
ggplot(abc_stock, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2) +
  labs(title = "Histogram: binwidth = 2")

5.2 Density plots

ggplot(abc_stock, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_density() +
  labs(title = "Density: Simulated stock price")

ggplot(abc_stock, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_density(fill = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Density with fill and alpha")

5.3 Grouped density

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = hwy, color = drv, fill = drv)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Highway MPG density by drive type")

5.4 Rug + histogram (density overlay)

library(MASS)
# mammal body sizes example
mam.new <- data.frame(body = log10(mammals$body))

ggplot(mam.new, aes(x = body)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 30) +
  geom_rug() +
  labs(title = "Histogram + rug: log10 body sizes (mammals)")
## Warning: The dot-dot notation (`..density..`) was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
## ℹ Please use `after_stat(density)` instead.
## This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
## Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
## generated.

5.5 Boxplots, violin plots, and stat_summary

# boxplot
ggplot(msleep, aes(x = vore, y = sleep_total)) +
  geom_boxplot(varwidth = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Boxplot: Sleep total by dietary vore")

# violin
ggplot(msleep, aes(x = vore, y = sleep_total)) +
  geom_violin(col = NA) +
  labs(title = "Violin: Sleep total by dietary vore")

# stat_summary example
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_sdl, fun.args = list(mult = 1), geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Mean and SD (approx) for Sepal.Length by Species")

5.6 2D density and tile

ggplot(faithful, aes(x = waiting, y = eruptions)) +
  stat_density_2d() +
  labs(title = "2D density: Old Faithful")

ggplot(faithful, aes(x = waiting, y = eruptions)) +
  stat_density_2d(geom = "tile", aes(fill = after_stat(density)), contour = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(title = "2D density tile (viridis)")

6.0 Visualizing Relationships Between Two Numerical Variables

6.1 Scatterplot baseline + grouped aesthetics

# baseline
p_base <- ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Displacement vs Highway MPG")

p_base

# grouped with color + shape
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = drv, shape = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Grouped linear fits by drive type")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

6.2 Overplotting remedies: alpha, jitter, 2D density

# alpha
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Scatter with alpha")

# jitter for discrete x
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +
  labs(title = "Jittered points by Species")

# 2D density tile
ggplot(faithful, aes(x = waiting, y = eruptions)) +
  stat_density_2d(geom = "tile", aes(fill = after_stat(density)), contour = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(title = "2D density tile")

6.3 Faceting and annotation

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = drv)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~drv) +
  labs(title = "Faceted linear fits by drive type")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

# annotation example
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 40, label = "Trend: decreasing hwy with displ", hjust = 0) +
  labs(title = "Annotated scatter plot")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

7.0 Multivariate and Specialized Visualizations

7.1 Multivariate aesthetic mapping example

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = drv, shape = drv, size = cyl)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75) +
  labs(title = "Multivariate encoding: displ, hwy, drv, cyl")

7.2 Pairwise matrix (GGally)

# Use a selection of numeric variables
#ggpairs(mpg[, c("displ", "hwy", "cty", "cyl")])

7.3 Ridgeline distributions (ggridges)

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = hwy, y = class, fill = class)) +
  geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.8, scale = 1) +
  labs(title = "Ridgeline: Highway MPG across classes")
## Picking joint bandwidth of 0.966

7.4 Specialized hybrids and hexbin

# violin + box
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = drv, y = hwy)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey95") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA) +
  labs(title = "Violin + box (hybrid)")

# hexbin
library(hexbin)

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
  geom_hex() +
  labs(title = "Hexbin plot: displ vs hwy")
